results.summary_before: This design replicates the classic 74181 4-bit slice ALU twice to form an 8-bit arithmetic logic unit, with an SPI slave peripheral for loading and reading registers and a multiplexer driving a 7-segment debug display. It supports all four SPI modes with eight configurable read/write registers and eight read-only status registers, and is controlled from an RP2040 using SPI1. Silicon reports confirm the SPI interface works when the SPI clock is at least five times slower than the ASIC clock, though the ALU itself was not verified by the independent tester. The project is notable as a faithful reproduction of a historic ALU part with a practical SPI debug interface.
results.summary: This design implements a Subleq CPU, a one-instruction set computer, using an external SPI FRAM for memory. It includes a UART interface with a baud rate of 115200 at a 10 MHz clock, and SPI signals for communicating with the FRAM. Testing involves loading compiled Subleq code into the FRAM via an Arduino and running the CPU. The documentation describes the Subleq architecture, toolchain, and external hardware requirements.
